subject.title: v2026.6.x system prompt bloat causes instruction following degradation on smaller models

question: Should OpenClaw solve this smaller-model prompt and skill-priority regression by changing default prompt/tool/skill composition, by extending existing opt-in lean and budget knobs, or by limiting the core response to documented workarounds while broader compaction remains separate?
rationale: Each plausible fix changes model-facing prompt priority, default tool exposure, skill-loading behavior, or config/default semantics, and those are compatibility-sensitive product choices under the repo policy.

options.title: Design coordinated prompt policy
options.body: Treat this as a core runtime/product issue and define one model-aware policy that composes prompt priority, localModelLean, Tool Search, skill budgets, and bootstrap limits before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to existing knobs
options.body: Keep the default runtime unchanged and improve docs or doctor guidance around localModelLean, tool allow/deny, bootstrap limits, and skill prompt budgets for constrained models.

options.title: Move remaining scope to compactor
options.body: Declare this issue covered by the broader context-compactor design and close only after the unique v2026.6 regression evidence is captured there.

recommendation.title: Design coordinated prompt policy
recommendation.body: Treat this as a core runtime/product issue and define one model-aware policy that composes prompt priority, localModelLean, Tool Search, skill budgets, and bootstrap limits before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current ownership signal is recent work on localModelLean and overlapping lean-mode mitigation PRs.
